title: Risk of metabolic complications in kidney transplantation after conversion to mTOR inhibitor: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text_summary: 本研究旨在评估肾脏移植后从环孢素A（CNI）转换为哺乳动物雷帕霉素靶点（mTOR）抑制剂后代谢并发症的风险。通过PubMed等数据库检索，纳入9项相关临床试验，共2323名患者。主要终点为移植后新发糖尿病（NODAT）和血脂异常的相对风险（RR）。结果显示，与CNI方案相比，mTOR抑制剂方案NODAT的RR为1.32（95%CI 0.92-1.87），血脂异常的RR为2.15（95%CI 1.35-3.41）。亚组分析显示，与西罗莫司和依维莫司方案、早期与晚期转换之间NODAT和血脂异常的发生率无差异。次要终点分析显示，mTOR抑制剂转换后急性排斥、蛋白尿和贫血的风险增加，但机会性感染的风险无差异。结论：CNI转换为mTOR抑制剂与NODAT风险增加的趋势和非显著相关，与血脂异常、急性排斥、蛋白尿和贫血的显著增加相关。临床医生应关注这些风险，并妥善管理以预防心血管并发症。
text:
Risk of Metabolic Complications in Kidney
Transplantation After Conversion to mTOR Inhibitor:
A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
N. Murakami1, L. V. Riella2,*,y and T. Funakoshi1,y
1Department of Medicine, Beth Israel Medical Center,
New York, NY
2Transplantation Research Center, Renal Division,
Brigham & Women’s Hospital, Boston Children’s
Hospital, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA
Corresponding author: Leonardo V. Riella,
lriella@rics.bwh.harvard.edu
yThese authors act as equivalent co-senior authors.
Mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors
have been used in transplantation with the hope of
minimizing calcineurin inhibitor (CNI)-induced neph-
rotoxicity. However, mTOR inhibitors are also associ-
ated with a range of side effects, including metabolic
complications. We aimed to determine the risks of
metabolic complications after the conversion from CNI
to mTOR inhibitor postkidney transplant. A systematic
search in PubMed up to September 2013 identiﬁed nine
relevant trials (a total of 2323 patients). The primary
end points were the relative risks (RRs) of new-onset
diabetes after transplant (NODAT) and hypercholes-
terolemia. The overall RRs of NODAT and hypercholes-
terolemia associated with mTOR inhibitors were 1.32
(95% conﬁdence interval [CI] 0.92–1.87) and 2.15 (95%
CI 1.35–3.41), respectively, compared with CNI-based
regimen. Subgroup analyses revealed no differences in
the incidence of NODAT or hypercholesterolemia
between sirolimus- versus everolimus-based regimen,
or between early versus late conversion. Analyses of
secondary outcomes revealed a higher risk of acute
rejection, proteinuria and anemia, but no difference in
the risk of opportunistic infections after mTOR inhibi-
tor conversion. In conclusion, the conversion from CNI
to mTOR inhibitor in low-to-moderate risk kidney
transplant recipients was associated with nonsigniﬁ-
cant trend toward increased risk of NODAT and
signiﬁcant increase in hypercholesterolemia, acute
rejection, proteinuria and anemia.

Introduction
Calcineurin inhibitor (CNI)-based regimens are most com-
monly
used
as
maintenance
regimens
after
kidney
transplantation because of their potent immunosuppres-
sive activity. However, long-term use of these agents has
been associated with signiﬁcant nephrotoxicity, which may
limit long-term graft and patient’s survival.
Recently, conversion from CNI-based regimen to mamma-
lian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitor-based regimen
in early (1–6 months) or late (6 months or later) posttrans-
plant has been tested in multiple trials, showing overall
improvement in graft function, though a high discontinua-
tion rate was observed in the mTOR inhibitor arm and some
trials reported a higher acute rejection rate (1–5).
Metabolic complications such as new-onset diabetes after
transplant (NODAT) (6–8) and hypercholesterolemia (9) have
been reported to be caused by both CNI and mTOR inhibitor
in postkidney transplant recipients. The overall incidence of
NODAT and hypercholesterolemia in posttransplant recip-
ients is as high as 15–30% and 40–44%, respectively (6,10),
which contributes to the high cardiovascular mortality and
death with a functioning graft (11). In fact, death with a
functioning graft is currently the most common cause of
graft loss long term. However, there has been a substantial
variation in the incidence of these metabolic complications
among different clinical trials, and no systematic attempt
has been reported to compare the incidence of metabolic
complications in CNI-based regimens with mTOR inhibitor-
based regimens in the setting of conversion.
Therefore, we performed a comprehensive literature
review and meta-analysis of randomized trials in which

CNI was switched to mTOR inhibitor after kidney trans-
plantation in order to assess the risk of developing NODAT
and hypercholesterolemia. As secondary outcomes, we
also evaluated the relative risks (RRs) of biopsy-proven
acute rejection (BPAR), proteinuria, anemia and opportu-
nistic infections upon mTOR inhibitor conversion.
Materials and Methods
Data source
We conducted an independent review of PubMed from January 1966 to
September 2013. Search keywords were: ‘‘sirolimus OR everolimus’’ AND
kidney transplant AND randomized controlled trial AND ‘‘conversion OR
minimization OR elimination.’’ An independent search of the Web of
Science, Embase and Cochrane electronic databases was also performed to
ensure that no additional clinical trials were overlooked. In cases of duplicate
publications, only the most complete, recent and updated report of the
clinical trial was included. When relevant data were unclear, efforts were
made to contact the corresponding authors. Finally, the most updated
package inserts of sirolimus (SRL) and everolimus (EVL) were reviewed to
identify relevant information (12,13).
Study selection
Trials were selected and systematically reviewed in accordance with the
Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses
(PRISMA) statement (14).
Clinical trials that met the following criteria were included (1) randomized
controlled trials (RCTs) in adult patients with kidney transplantation; (2) trials
focusing on conversion from CNI to mTOR inhibitors, either SRL or EVL,
early (<6 months posttransplant) or late (>6 months) phase of transplanta-
tion; and (3) events or event rate and sample size available for metabolic
complications including NODAT and hypercholesterolemia. The studies
were excluded if mTOR inhibitors were used as de novo immunosuppres-
sants, or combined with CNIs, since de novo use of mTOR inhibitors are
known to be associated with high rate of discontinuation, marked proteinuria
and less common in use these days (15–17). Also excluded were those with
very late conversion (>10 years posttransplant). Independent reviewers
screened reports that included the key term by their titles and abstracts for
relevance. Then, full texts of the relevant articles were retrieved to assess
eligibility. The references of relevant reports were also reviewed manually.
Data extraction and clinical end points
Two investigators (NM and TF) independently performed data extraction.
Any discrepancies between reviewers were resolved by consensus. The
following information was recorded for each study: ﬁrst author’s name, year of
publication, number of patients enrolled, treatment arms, median age, incidence
of diabetes at baseline, timing of conversion from CNI to mTOR inhibitor, follow-
up period, number of events of NODAT and hypercholesterolemia (Table 1).
The numbers of patients evaluable for metabolic complications were utilized
as the number analyses for each trial, unless this was not indicated in the
publication, in which case, the number of patients enrolled was utilized. In
selected clinical trials, diagnosis of criteria of NODAT and hypercholesterolemia
were recorded according to the guidelines (18,19). More speciﬁcally, NODAT
was deﬁned as hemoglobin A1c (HgbA1c) >6.5%, fasting plasma glucose
>126mg/dL and/or 2-h plasma glucose >200mg/dL after a 75-g oral glucose
tolerance test (OGTT), and hypercholesterolemia was deﬁned as total
cholesterol >200mg/dL or LDL >100mg/dL. As secondary end points, we
evaluated the risks of development of BPAR, proteinuria, anemia and
opportunistic infections (Table 1).
The quality of included trials was rated using the 5-point Jadad scale (1 [poor]
to 5 [excellent]), which is based on the reporting of randomization method,
blinding method, withdrawals and dropouts (20).
Statistical analysis
The primary outcomes were incidence and RR with 95% conﬁdence
intervals (CIs) of NODAT and hypercholesterolemia. The secondary
outcomes were level of serum total cholesterol, triglyceride, Hgb and
proteinuria (continuous outcomes) as well as incidence and RR of acute
rejection, and opportunistic infections. For the calculation of incidence, the
number of patients with each adverse event and the number of patients
receiving mTOR inhibitor as a substitute for CNI or to maintaining CNI was
utilized. The proportion of patients with these adverse outcomes and 95%
CIs were derived from each trial. We also calculated the RRs and CIs
comparing the incidence of each adverse event in patients assigned to
mTOR inhibitor as a substitute for CNI with those assigned to continuation of
CNI in the same trial. To calculate 95% CIs, the variance of a log-transformed
study-speciﬁc RR was derived using the delta method. The continuous
outcomes (such as serum triglyceride, total cholesterol, Hgb, leukocytes
and platelets) were assessed using the mean difference with 95% CI, or
the standardized mean difference if different scales were used (e.g.
proteinuria).
Statistical heterogeneity in results between trials included in the meta-
analysis was examined using Cochrane’s Q statistic, and inconsistency was
quantiﬁed with I2 statistic [100%  (Q  df)/Q], which estimates the
percentage of total variation across studies due to heterogeneity rather
than chance (21). The assumption of homogeneity was considered invalid for
p-values less than 0.10. Summary incidence, RRs were calculated using
random-effects or ﬁxed-effects models depending on the heterogeneity of
included studies. When substantial heterogeneity was observed, the pooled
estimate calculated based on the random-effects model was reported.
Otherwise, results from the ﬁxed-effects model were reported. Prespeciﬁed
subgroup analyses were performed for the primary outcomes according to
mTOR inhibitor type (SRL vs. EVL), timing of conversion from CNI to mTOR
inhibitor (<6 months posttransplant vs. >6 months) and length of follow-up
(1 year vs. 2 years). Differences between these subgroups were assessed
using Q statistics. We evaluated publication bias using funnel plots and with
the Begg and Egger tests (22,23). A two-tailed p-value of less than 0.05 was
considered statistically signiﬁcant. Statistical analyses were performed by
using the program Review Manager 5.1 (Nordic Cochrane Centre, Cochrane
Collaboration, Copenhagen, Denmark) and Comprehensive MetaAnalysis
program (Version 2; Biostat, Englewood, NJ).
Results
Search results
Our search strategy yielded 109 potentially relevant publica-
tions in PubMed. Figure 1 outlines the selection process and
reasons for study exclusion. We identiﬁed one article in
the references of relevant reports that was not previously
identiﬁed in PubMed (24). A total of nine open-label RCTs (1–
4,24–28) were selected for the meta-analysis, including seven
trials reporting NODAT and nine trials reporting hypercholes-
terolemia. The onset of NODAT and hyperlipidemia was
not clariﬁed in one study (26), in which we considered the
reported cases as new-onset events after randomization and
included them in the study. Other studies clearly documented
the incidences of complications after randomization. Three
additional studies, which did not describe the incidence of
NODAT and hypercholesterolemia, were further included in

last 10 years with the majority between 2009 and 2013.
Most of the studies had the Jadad score of 3, with a mean of
2.9 (good) indicating that the overall study quality was fair
(Table 1).
For secondary outcomes, a total of 15 open-label random-
ized trials were selected for analyses (1–4,24–34), as
described in Table 1.
Population characteristics
A total of 2323 patients (SRL: 916, EVL: 384, controls: 1023)
were available for the meta-analysis. All patients underwent
kidney transplant, switched from CNI to mTOR inhibitor in
early (ﬁve trials, <6 months posttransplant) or late phase
(four trials, >6 months posttransplant). The immunological
risk of transplant was low-moderate in six trials (panel-
reactive
antibody <30%), while
the others did
not
described the immunological risks in detail. For induction
therapy, two trials used basiliximab, one trial used anti-
thymocyte globulin, one trial used daclizumab and the
others did not speciﬁcally described induction therapy. For
concomitant immunosuppressive regimens, all trials used
combination
of
CNI,
anti-metabolites
(mycophenolate
mofetil [MMF]/mycophenolic acid [MPA] or azathioprine
[Aza]) and steroids. The baseline characteristics in each trial
are presented in Table 1.
Primary outcomes
Incidence and RR of NODAT:
We included a total of
2083 patients (mTOR inhibitors: 1179; controls: 904) from
seven RCTs. The incidence of NODAT in patients receiving
mTOR inhibitor was 5.5% (95% CI 3.26–9.3) (Figure 2). The
test for heterogeneity was signiﬁcant and a random-effects
model was used (Q ¼ 19.80; p ¼ 0.003; I2 ¼ 69.69). For the
control arm, the incidence was 5.05% (95% CI 3.3–7.7)
using the random-effects model (heterogeneity test:
Q ¼ 10.69; p ¼ 0.099; I2 ¼ 45.85). There was no signiﬁcant
increase in the risk of NODAT with the use of mTOR
inhibitors compared with the controls (RR 1.32; 95% CI
0.92–1.87; p ¼ 0.13; Figure 2). The ﬁxed-effects model was
used because there was no signiﬁcant heterogeneity
(Q ¼ 3.68; p ¼ 0.72; I2 ¼ 0.0).
Incidence and RR of hypercholesterolemia:
A total of
2323 patients (mTOR inhibitors: 1300; controls: 1023) from
nine RCTs were available. The incidence of hypercholes-
terolemia due to mTOR inhibitors was 30.5% (95% CI 16.2–
49.9) using the random-effects model (heterogeneity test:
Q ¼ 218.78; p < 0.001; I2 ¼ 96.34). For the control arm, the

Mean difference in triglyceride and total cholesterol
levels after conversion:
A total of 1399 patients (mTOR
inhibitors: 702; controls: 697) from eight RCTs were
available for mean difference analyses of triglyceride and
total cholesterol level. Triglyceride and total cholesterol
level were higher in mTOR inhibitor group by 47.4 mg/dL
(95% CI 37.5–57.3) and 28.9 mg/dL (95% CI 20.7–37.1),
respectively (Figure 3B and C).
Subgroup analyses:
We performed subgroup analyses
of SRL- versus EVL-treated patients in trials converting CNI
to mTOR inhibitor early (<6 months posttransplant) versus
late (>6 months) as well as in trials with short (1 year)
versus long (2 years) follow-up. No signiﬁcant differences
were observed for RR of NODAT (1.33 vs. 1.10; p ¼ 0.73) or
hypercholesterolemia (1.95 vs. 2.55; p ¼ 0.50) between
patients treated with SRL or EVL, respectively. Similarly, no
differences were found for RR of NODAT (1.12 vs. 1.34;
p ¼ 0.72) or hypercholesterolemia (2.10 vs. 2.01; p ¼ 0.90)
between trials with short or long follow-up. Finally, patients
enrolled onto early conversion trials did not demonstrate
any difference in RR of NODAT (0.93 vs. 1.61; p ¼ 0.14) or
hypercholesterolemia (1.84 vs. 2.23; p ¼ 0.63) compared
with those enrolled onto late conversion trials. Given that
tacrolimus is known to be more diabetogenic compared
with cyclosporine (CsA) (35), it was of great interest to
compare RRs of NODAT between CNIs used before
conversion. However, most of the articles included in this
study did not describe the incidence of NODAT separately
based on CNI usage and subgroup analysis was not
performed.
Secondary outcomes
BPAR and proteinuria:
As graft outcome measures, RRs
of BPAR and standardized mean difference analysis of
proteinuria were performed. Standardized mean difference
analysis was used for assessment of proteinuria since
proteinuria was reported in different scales depending on
the study, such as gram/day, gram/gram creatinine, gram/
millimole creatinine. A total of 2892 patients (mTOR
inhibitors: 1603, controls: 1289) from 14 RCTs were
included. The incidences of BPAR were 10.7% (95% CI
7.61–14.7) and 7.1% (95% CI 5.2–9.7) for mTOR inhibitor
and control group, respectively. The risk of BPAR was
signiﬁcantly higher with mTOR inhibitors compared with
CNIs (RR 1.52; 95% CI 1.19–1.94; p < 0.001; Figure 4A). For
the standardized mean difference analysis of proteinuria, a
total of 2027 patients (mTOR inhibitors: 1096, controls: 931)
from 10 RCTs were included. The degree of proteinuria was
signiﬁcantly higher in the mTOR inhibitor group (standard-
ized mean difference 0.23, 95% CI 0.15–0.32; p < 0.001;
Figure 4B).
Hematological complications:
A total of 1301 patients
(mTOR inhibitors: 648, controls: 653) from seven RCTs
were included for mean difference analysis of Hgb level.
Hgb was signiﬁcantly lower in mTOR inhibitor group
(0.37 g/dL, 95% CI 0.67 to 0.08; p ¼ 0.01) compared
with control group (Figure 4C). Leukocyte and platelet
numbers were reported only in three studies and there was
no signiﬁcant difference in their numbers by mean
difference analysis (data not shown).
Opportunistic infections:
A total of 2503 patients
(mTOR inhibitors: 1412, controls: 1091) from 10 RCTs
were included. Opportunistic infections were deﬁned as
infections by cytomegalovirus (CMV), BK/polyoma virus,
herpes
simplex
virus,
herpes
zoster
virus,
Candida,
Aspergillus, Pneumocystis jiroveci or Cryptococcus. The
incidences of opportunistic infections were 11.6% (95% CI
8.63–15.5) and 12.1% (95% CI 7.7–18.4) for mTOR inhibitor
group and CNI group, respectively. There was no signiﬁcant

We found no evidence of publication
bias for RR of NODAT and hypercholesterolemia and

However, the Begg tests showed no evidence of bias

Discussion
To our knowledge, this is the ﬁrst meta-analysis to evaluate
the risk of metabolic complications associated with
conversion from CNIs to mTOR inhibitors in postkidney
transplant recipients in contemporary immunosuppressive
regimens. Our results showed that the conversion from

CNI to mTOR inhibitors did not decrease the risk of NODAT
(RR 1.32; 95% CI 0.92–1.87; p ¼ 0.13) and was actually
associated with a nonstatistically signiﬁcant increase in
NODAT.
An increase in risk of NODAT associated with SRL was
demonstrated in a large registry study using data of the
United States Renal Data System from 1995 to 2003.
Among 20 124 adult recipients of a ﬁrst kidney transplant
without diabetes, patients treated with SRL in combination
with an anti-metabolite (MMF or Aza) were at increased risk
for NODAT (hazard ratio 1.36; 95% CI 1.09–1.69; p < 0.01),
compared with patients treated with CsA and an anti-
metabolite (37). However, as with any clinical registry-
based analysis, there is a fundamental limitation on integrity
of data due to the use of diagnostic codes. Furthermore, the
analysis was relatively old, and the results may not be easily
applicable in accordance with recent advances in immuno-
suppressant management, including the use of lower CNI
dose for long-term maintenance (38). Our study, by
focusing on more recent studies published within the last
10 years, reﬂects more contemporary use of immunosup-
pressive agents. However, our study did include patients
receiving CsA-based regimen. Unfortunately, we were not
able to perform a separate analysis between CsA and
tacrolimus-treated patients due to lack of details on the
included studies about complications in those subgroups.
Given the higher incidence of BPAR in the mTOR inhibitor-
based regimen (Figure 4A), the use of steroids for
treatment of acute rejection could be contributing to the
increased risk of NODAT in this group. However, due to the
lack of data on steroid use in individual trials, we are unable
to further investigate this potential cofounder in this meta-
analysis. Another important consideration is related to
the impact of higher immunosuppression drug levels in
the development of metabolic complications, as it has
been previously shown in multiple studies with CNI
minimization protocols (39). Though we attempted to
capture
immunosuppression
drug
levels,
there
was

proteinuria (B) and hemoglobin (C) and RR of opportunistic infections (D).

signiﬁcant heterogeneity of reporting (trough vs. C2 levels)
and missing data of actual immunosuppressive drug levels
in many trials prevented appropriate evaluation of this
question.
The exact mechanisms by which mTOR inhibitors cause
NODAT have not been clearly deﬁned; however, pro-
posed mechanisms include: impaired insulin-mediated
suppression of hepatic glucose production (40), increased
insulin resistance and/or direct beta cell toxicity (41–43).
Indeed,
renal
transplant
patients
tested
for
insulin
sensitivity before and after conversion from a CNI to
SRL had a signiﬁcant reduction in insulin sensitivity and
beta cell function (44). Though our study did not show a
signiﬁcant increase in NODAT after conversion, we may
conclude at least that mTOR inhibitors are as diabetogenic
as CNIs.
We also revealed a signiﬁcantly higher risk of hypercholes-
terolemia with mTOR inhibitor-based regimens than CNI-
based regimens. A systematic review on mTOR versus
non-mTOR inhibitor immunosuppressive treatment regi-
mens in renal transplant recipients summarized dyslipide-
mia associated with mTOR inhibitors. In the review, 10 of
the 17 included RCTs reported signiﬁcantly higher levels of
cholesterol in mTOR inhibitor groups than in non-mTOR
inhibitor groups (45).
Recent studies showed possible mechanisms of hyper-
cholesterolemia associated with mTOR inhibitor use, which
may
include:
inhibition
of
adipogenesis
and
hepatic
lipogenesis via inhibition of mTOR complex 1 and nuclear
accumulation of transcription factor sterol regulatory
element-binding proteins; and inhibition of hepatic lipolysis
via mTOR complex 2 (46,47).
Management of metabolic complications posttransplant
has been of great interest in order to reduce cardiovascular
morbidity and mortality. NODAT has been repeatedly
reported to be an independent risk of increased cardiovas-
cular events (6,48). Screening of posttransplant hypergly-
cemia/NODAT using fasting plasma glucose (or preferably
OGTT) and early intervention using oral hypoglycemic
agents and/or insulin, targeting HgbA1c <7% are recom-
mended (49). Management of hyperglycemia posttrans-
plant
involves
both
attempting
to
minimize
any
immunosuppressive drug contributing to diabetes (individ-
ualized decision based on risk of rejection) and initiation of
conventional glucose-lowering therapies (oral hypoglyce-
mic agents or insulin regimens). Similarly, the association

between hypercholesterolemia and cardiovascular risk has
been examined in multiple randomized trials. The ALERT
study showed a potential beneﬁt of lowering LDL by statin,
decreasing cardiovascular risks (50,51). These ﬁndings
were reinforced by the SHARP study (52). Following the
recommendations about dyslipidemia management in the
general population, the most recently updated KDIGO lipid
management guideline suggests that statin therapy should
be initiated in all kidney transplant recipients, irrespective of
cholesterol levels (53). Nonetheless, this conclusion is
based on weak data and further studies are warranted.
Switching from CNI to mTOR inhibitor has multiple
potential beneﬁts, including avoidance of CNI-induced
nephrotoxicity and hypertension (54) and reduction in
malignancies, in particular of skin origin (55). However,
contemporary trials looking at mTOR conversion failed to
demonstrate an improvement in renal function long
term (30,34). In addition, a high degree of discontinuation
of mTOR inhibitors was observed in most trials due to
multiple side effects including aphthous stomatitis, edema,
pneumonitis, proteinuria, diarrhea and anemia. Indeed, our
secondary outcome analyses revealed increased risks of
BPAR, proteinuria and anemia (Figure 4A–C). Notably, our
subgroup analysis showed no difference between SRL and
EVL in the incidence of NODAT and hypercholesterolemia
after conversion. However, since there has been only a
relatively small number of RCTs using EVL as a substitute
for CNI, deﬁnitive conclusions cannot be made based on
current data. The ideal patients that might beneﬁt from
conversion are still unclear, though it is generally accepted
that low immunological risk patients with estimated GFR
>40 mL/min and no signiﬁcant proteinuria (<500 mg/day)
are potentially good candidates, in particular those with
high-risk for skin malignancies or with signiﬁcant vascular
complications.
Our study has several potential limitations. First, as with any
meta-analysis, the results described here are affected by the
limitations of individual clinical trials that were selected for
this meta-analysis. Second, this is a meta-analysis at study
level; therefore confounding variables at the patient level
were not incorporated into the analysis. Thus, we could not
establish risk factors associated with the development of
metabolic complications. Third, there is a substantial
heterogeneity of the studies included. Some had small,
pilot-study design without precalculated sample size. Even
though we were not able to detect difference in risk of
NODAT between mTOR inhibitor-based regimen and CNI-
based regimen, this result may be due to the heterogeneity
of the studies.
In conclusion, our meta-analysis has demonstrated that
conversion from CNI to mTOR inhibitor in early or late
posttransplant is associated with nonsigniﬁcant trend
toward an increased risk of NODAT and a signiﬁcantly
higher risk of hypercholesterolemia. Since death with a
functioning graft is the most common cause of long-term
graft loss, clinicians should be aware of these risks and
manage them properly in order to prevent cardiovascular
complications.

- **B部分**：标题为“Triglyceride”，展示mTOR抑制剂组与对照组甘油三酯水平的均值差异（Mean Difference）。数据包含各研究的“均值（Mean）”“标准差（SD）”“总人数（Total）”“权重（Weight）”，以及加权均值差和95%CI。关键趋势：汇总分析显示，mTOR抑制剂组甘油三酯水平比对照组高47.42（95%CI 37.53 - 57.31），研究间异质性较低（I²=23%）。  

- **C部分**：标题为“Total cholesterol”，展示mTOR抑制剂组与对照组总胆固醇水平的均值差异。数据结构与B部分一致，关键趋势：汇总分析显示，mTOR抑制剂组总胆固醇水平比对照组高28.93（95%CI 20.73 - 37.13），研究间异质性中等（I²=62%）。

图4包含A、B两部分，均为森林图（属于数据图表，用于荟萃分析结果展示）：  
- **A部分**：标题为“Rate of biopsy - proven Acute Rejection”。图表类型是森林图，展示不同研究（Study or Subgroup）中mTOR抑制剂组与对照组的活检证实急性排斥事件数（Events）、总人数（Total），以及风险比（Risk Ratio）及其95%置信区间（95%CI）。关键趋势为：整体风险比（Total）为1.52，95%CI [1.19, 1.94]，提示mTOR抑制剂组活检证实急性排斥的风险高于对照组，且整体效应有统计学意义（P = 0.0008）。  
- **B部分**：标题为“Proteinuria”。图表类型是森林图，展示不同研究中的蛋白尿均值（Mean）、标准差（SD）、总人数（Total），以及标准化均数差（Std. Mean Difference）及其95%置信区间（95%CI）。关键趋势为：整体标准化均数差为0.23，95%CI [0.15, 0.32]，提示mTOR抑制剂组的蛋白尿水平高于对照组，且整体效应有统计学意义（P < 0.00001）。

图5包含两个子图（C和D），均为森林图（meta分析图）：  
- **C图（Hemoglobin）**：展示不同研究中mTOR抑制剂组与对照组的血红蛋白水平数据。表格列出了各研究的mTOR抑制剂组与对照组的均值（Mean）、标准差（SD）、总样本量（Total）、权重（Weight），以及均数差（Mean Difference）和95%置信区间（95%CI）；右侧森林图以横轴表示均数差（范围-10~10），显示各研究的效应值及总体效应（菱形标记）。关键趋势：总体均数差为-0.37，95%CI[-0.67, -0.08]，P=0.01，提示mTOR抑制剂组血红蛋白水平显著低于对照组。  
- **D图（RR of opportunistic infections）**：展示不同研究中mTOR抑制剂组与对照组的机会性感染风险（以比值比Odds Ratio表示）数据。表格列出了各研究的mTOR抑制剂组与对照组的事件数（Events）、总样本量（Total）、权重，以及比值比（Odds Ratio）和95%置信区间（95%CI）；右侧森林图以横轴表示比值比（范围0.01~100），显示各研究的效应值及总体效应（菱形标记）。关键趋势：总体比值比为0.94，95%CI[0.73, 1.22]，P=0.66，提示两组机会性感染风险无显著差异。
